```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-load}
mod_name <- "Penland_2024_sodiumZirconiumCyclosilicate"
mod <- readModelDb(mod_name)
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-024-01360-9> (open access; the
  model equations and covariate functional forms are in its Electronic
  Supplementary Material)

Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) is a non-absorbed oral potassium binder.
No drug concentration can be measured, so the authors drive the effect with a
virtual exposure (a K-PD compartment): each dose enters `depot_kpd` and is
eliminated first-order with mean transit time 137 h. The exposure is scaled so
that a steady-state 1 g once-daily (QD) regimen has a mean 24-h exposure of 1;
EC50 is therefore expressed as a QD dose in grams. Serum potassium follows an
indirect-response model,

$$\frac{dSK}{dt} = K_{in} - K_{out} \cdot SK, \qquad
K_{in} = BL \cdot K_{out} \cdot placebo \cdot
\left(1 - \frac{I_{max} \cdot SZC^{h}}{SZC^{h} + EC_{50}^{h}}\right),$$

with $SK(0) = BL$, the observed baseline serum potassium at the first dose.

# Population

The analysis pooled 2369 patients with hyperkalemia (screening serum potassium
> 5.0 mmol/L) and 25,764 serum potassium observations from seven phase II/III
SZC studies (ZS-002, ZS-003, ZS-004, ZS-005, D9480C00002, D9482C00001,
D9482C00002; Table 1 and Supplementary Table S1). Mean (SD) age was 66.0 (12)
years, 61% were male, 68% White, 9% Black/African American, 21% Asian and 2%
other race; 34% had congestive heart failure and 62% diabetes. Mean (SD)
baseline serum potassium was 5.49 (0.43) mmol/L and MDRD eGFR 45.9 (29)
mL/min/1.73 m^2. Correction-phase dosing was 0-15 g three times daily (TID) for
48-72 h, and maintenance dosing 0-15 g QD for up to 28 days.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Penland_2024_sodiumZirconiumCyclosilicate")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value is from Table 2 ("Full model" column) of Penland 2024; the
equations and functional forms are from the Supplementary Methods.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `d/dt(depot_kpd) = -kel * depot_kpd` | n/a | Supplementary Methods, dSZC/dt |
| `exposure = depot_kpd * kel * 24` | n/a | Methods "Base Model": exposure scaled to 1 for steady-state 1 g QD |
| `d/dt(serum_k) = kin - kout * serum_k`, `serum_k(0) = POT` | n/a | Supplementary Methods, dSK/dt and SK(0) = BL |
| `kin = POT * kout * plac * (1 - inh)` | n/a | Supplementary Methods, Kin equation |
| Continuous covariates: power `(cov / ref)^theta` | n/a | Supplementary Methods (power form); see Assumptions |
| Categorical covariates: `exp(theta * cov)` | n/a | Supplementary Methods (proportional shift) |
| `lkel` = log(1/137) | MTT 137 h | Table 2, SZC MTT |
| `lkout` | 0.548 1/h | Table 2, Serum K+ Kout |
| `lplac` | 0.923 | Table 2, Placebo effect on Kin |
| `limax` | 0.633 | Table 2, Emax (% inhibition) 63.3 |
| `lec50` | 32.8 g | Table 2, EC50 |
| `lhill` | 1.36 | Table 2, Hill coefficient |
| `e_pot_ec50` | -1.04 | Table 2, BL covariate on EC50 |
| `e_age_ec50` | -0.486 | Table 2, Age covariate on EC50 |
| `e_wt_ec50` | 0.515 | Table 2, Body weight covariate on EC50 |
| `e_crcl_ec50` | 0.316 | Table 2, eGFR covariate on EC50 |
| `e_race_black_ec50` | -0.325 | Table 2, Black/African American covariate on EC50 |
| `e_race_asian_ec50` | -0.134 | Table 2, Asian covariate on EC50 |
| `e_race_other_ec50` | -0.122 | Table 2, 'Other' race covariate on EC50 |
| `e_pot_plac` | 0.44 | Table 2, BL covariate on placebo |
| `e_crcl_plac` | 0.0371 | Table 2, eGFR covariate on placebo |
| `e_dis_chf_plac` | 0.00121 | Table 2, Heart failure status covariate on placebo |
| `e_dis_diab_plac` | -0.0133 | Table 2, Diabetes status covariate on placebo |
| `e_sexf_kout` | 0.254 | Table 2, Sex covariate on Kout |
| `etalplac` | 0.00296 | Table 2, BPV of placebo variance (log-normal) |
| `etalec50` | 0.171 | Table 2, BPV of EC50 variance (log-normal) |
| `addSd` | sqrt(0.118) mmol/L | Table 2, Residual error variance; additive (Supplementary Methods) |

# Simulation helpers

The paper's covariate and dose-response predictions are means over
between-patient variability. To make every number below reproducible on any
machine, the between-patient random effects are drawn in base R (seeded with
`set.seed()`) and passed to `rxSolve()` through `params`, with the model's own
random effects zeroed. The EC50 effects are placed on a deterministic normal
quantile grid.

```{r helpers}
mod_fixed <- suppressMessages(rxode2::zeroRe(mod))
th <- ui$theta
om <- diag(ui$omega)

ref_patient <- data.frame(
  POT = 5.4, AGE = 65, WT = 85, CRCL = 45,
  RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0, RACE_OTHER = 0,
  DIS_CHF = 0, DIS_DIAB = 0, SEXF = 0
)

# Regimen: `corr` g TID for 48 h (6 doses), then `maint` g every `maint_ii` h
# from 48 h for 28 days. Observations of the serum_k state at the end of the
# correction phase (48 h) and at day 28 of maintenance (48 + 672 h).
t_corr <- 48
t_maint <- 48 + 28 * 24
make_events <- function(cov, corr, maint = 0, maint_ii = 24, regimen,
                        obs_times = c(0, t_corr, t_maint)) {
  n <- nrow(cov)
  dose_times <- c(seq(0, 40, by = 8), if (maint > 0) seq(48, 48 + 27 * 24, by = maint_ii))
  dose_amt <- c(rep(corr, 6), if (maint > 0) rep(maint, length(seq(48, 48 + 27 * 24, by = maint_ii))))
  doses <- data.frame(time = dose_times, amt = dose_amt, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot_kpd") |>
    dplyr::filter(amt > 0)
  obs <- data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "serum_k")
  one <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs)
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = cov$id, one) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cov, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = regimen) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

solve_fixed <- function(events, etas) {
  pars <- data.frame(
    id = etas$id,
    etalec50 = etas$etalec50,
    etalplac = etas$etalplac
  )
  # The random effects arrive through `params`, so rxode2's warning that the
  # zeroed model has no omega to sample from is expected; any other warning
  # still propagates.
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fixed, events, params = pars, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w))) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
```

# Structural checks

## Exposure scaling

The authors scale the virtual exposure so that a steady-state 1 g QD regimen
has a mean 24-h exposure of 1 (Methods, "Base Model"). With
`exposure = depot_kpd * kel * 24` the mean over a dosing interval at steady
state equals the QD dose in grams exactly; this checks it numerically for 10 g
QD.

```{r exposure-check}
# The grid is offset from the dose times so that no observation coincides
# with a dose; the one dosing interval it spans adds < 2e-4 trapezoid error.
ev_ss <- rxode2::et(amt = 10, ii = 24, addl = 120, cmt = "depot_kpd") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(99 * 24 + 0.025, 100 * 24 + 0.025, by = 0.05))
ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fixed, ev_ss, params = ref_patient, returnType = "data.frame")
mean_exposure <- sum(diff(ss$time) * (head(ss$exposure, -1) + tail(ss$exposure, -1)) / 2) / 24
mean_exposure
# Same parameters on both sides (a solve against its own closed form), so the
# tolerance reflects only integration and trapezoid error.
stopifnot(abs(mean_exposure - 10) / 10 < 1e-3)
```

## Placebo steady state

Without SZC, `kin = POT * kout * plac`, so serum potassium relaxes from its
baseline to `POT * plac`; for the reference patient (baseline 5.4 mmol/L) this
is 5.4 x 0.923 = 4.98 mmol/L, the plateau of the 0 g panel of Figure 3.

```{r placebo-ss}
ev_pbo <- rxode2::et(seq(0, 240, by = 24))
pbo <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fixed, ev_pbo, params = ref_patient, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(
  abs(pbo$serum_k[1] - 5.4) < 1e-8,
  abs(tail(pbo$serum_k, 1) - 5.4 * exp(th[["lplac"]])) < 1e-4
)
tail(pbo$serum_k, 1)
```

# Reference-patient covariate effects (Figure 4 and Results text)

The reference patient is a nondiabetic, non-CHF White male aged 65 years with
eGFR 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2, body weight 85 kg and baseline serum potassium
5.4 mmol/L. Each covariate profile below changes one value from the reference
and reports the placebo-adjusted change from baseline after 48 h of 10 g TID
(correction phase) and after a further 28 days of 10 g QD (maintenance phase),
averaged over the EC50 and placebo between-patient variability (200 effects on
a normal quantile grid, `set.seed()` for the placebo effect pairing).

```{r fig4-profiles}
n_eta <- 200
set.seed(20240319)
eta_grid <- data.frame(
  etalec50 = qnorm((seq_len(n_eta) - 0.5) / n_eta) * sqrt(om[["etalec50"]]),
  etalplac = sample(qnorm((seq_len(n_eta) - 0.5) / n_eta)) * sqrt(om[["etalplac"]])
)

profiles <- list(
  "Reference patient" = list(),
  "Potassium baseline: 6 mmol/L" = list(POT = 6),
  "Potassium baseline: 5 mmol/L" = list(POT = 5),
  "eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73 m2" = list(CRCL = 88),
  "eGFR: 17 mL/min/1.73 m2" = list(CRCL = 17),
  "Diabetes mellitus" = list(DIS_DIAB = 1),
  "Congestive heart failure" = list(DIS_CHF = 1),
  "Body weight: 111 kg" = list(WT = 111),
  "Body weight: 57 kg" = list(WT = 57),
  "Black/African American" = list(RACE_BLACK = 1),
  "Asian" = list(RACE_ASIAN = 1),
  "Age: 81 years" = list(AGE = 81),
  "Age: 49 years" = list(AGE = 49)
)

profile_cov <- function(k) {
  cov <- ref_patient
  for (nm in names(profiles[[k]])) cov[[nm]] <- profiles[[k]][[nm]]
  cov <- cov[rep(1, n_eta), ]
  cov$id <- (k - 1L) * n_eta + seq_len(n_eta)
  cov$profile <- names(profiles)[k]
  cov
}
prof_cov <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(profiles), profile_cov))
prof_eta <- cbind(id = prof_cov$id, eta_grid[rep(seq_len(n_eta), length(profiles)), ])

# Active arm and the placebo comparator share covariates and random effects;
# the comparator for the maintenance phase also received 10 g TID for 48 h.
ev_act <- make_events(prof_cov, corr = 10, maint = 10, regimen = "active")
ev_pbo_c <- make_events(prof_cov, corr = 0, regimen = "placebo") |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = id + 10000L)
ev_pbo_m <- make_events(prof_cov, corr = 10, regimen = "placebo_maint") |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = id + 20000L)
ev_prof <- dplyr::bind_rows(ev_act, ev_pbo_c, ev_pbo_m)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_prof[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
eta_prof <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  prof_eta,
  dplyr::mutate(prof_eta, id = id + 10000L),
  dplyr::mutate(prof_eta, id = id + 20000L)
)

sim_prof <- solve_fixed(ev_prof, eta_prof) |>
  dplyr::mutate(base_id = id %% 10000L) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(prof_cov, id, profile), by = c("base_id" = "id"))

prof_tab <- sim_prof |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(t_corr, t_maint)) |>
  dplyr::select(base_id, profile, regimen, time, serum_k) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = regimen, values_from = serum_k) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pa_cfb = ifelse(time == t_corr, active - placebo, active - placebo_maint),
    phase = ifelse(time == t_corr, "correction", "maintenance")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(profile, phase) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pa_cfb = mean(pa_cfb), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = phase, values_from = pa_cfb)

# Correction-phase values stated in the Results text of Penland 2024.
published_corr <- tibble::tribble(
  ~profile, ~published,
  "Reference patient", -0.48,
  "eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73 m2", -0.37,
  "eGFR: 17 mL/min/1.73 m2", -0.71,
  "Black/African American", -0.69,
  "Asian", -0.55,
  "Congestive heart failure", -0.48,
  "Diabetes mellitus", -0.49
)

fig4_cmp <- prof_tab |>
  dplyr::left_join(published_corr, by = "profile") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (correction - published) / published) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(profile, names(profiles)))

fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Covariate profile" = profile,
    "Correction 48 h, simulated (mmol/L)" = correction,
    "Correction 48 h, published (mmol/L)" = published,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff,
    "Maintenance day 28, simulated (mmol/L)" = maintenance
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Placebo-adjusted serum K+ change from baseline with SZC 10 g (Penland 2024 Figure 4 and Results).")
```

```{r fig4-check}
chk4 <- dplyr::filter(fig4_cmp, !is.na(published))
stopifnot(nrow(chk4) == nrow(published_corr))
# Deterministic: the random effects are a fixed grid and the covariates are
# fixed, so the only noise is the integrator. A mis-transcribed EC50, Imax,
# exponent or exposure scaling moves these values by far more than 10%.
stopifnot(max(abs(chk4$pct_diff)) < 10)
```

The paper also states that the 5 g and 15 g responses of the reference
patient span -0.21 to -0.76 mmol/L in the correction phase.

```{r fig4-range}
cov_ref <- ref_patient[rep(1, n_eta), ]
cov_ref$id <- seq_len(n_eta)
eta_ref <- cbind(id = cov_ref$id, eta_grid)
corr_mean <- function(dose) {
  act <- solve_fixed(make_events(cov_ref, corr = dose, regimen = "a"), eta_ref)
  pbo <- solve_fixed(make_events(cov_ref, corr = 0, regimen = "p"), eta_ref)
  mean(act$serum_k[act$time == t_corr] - pbo$serum_k[pbo$time == t_corr])
}
# The random effects passed through `params` must reach the solve: EC50 of
# the reference patient is exactly exp(lec50 + etalec50).
chk_ec50 <- solve_fixed(make_events(cov_ref, corr = 10, regimen = "a"), eta_ref) |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, ec50)
stopifnot(
  nrow(chk_ec50) == n_eta,
  max(abs(chk_ec50$ec50 / exp(th[["lec50"]] + eta_ref$etalec50) - 1)) < 1e-10
)
range_sim <- c("5 g" = corr_mean(5), "15 g" = corr_mean(15))
range_sim
stopifnot(
  abs(range_sim[["5 g"]] - (-0.21)) / 0.21 < 0.10,
  abs(range_sim[["15 g"]] - (-0.76)) / 0.76 < 0.10
)
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
prof_tab |>
  dplyr::filter(profile != "Reference patient") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(correction, maintenance), names_to = "phase", values_to = "pa_cfb") |>
  dplyr::mutate(profile = factor(profile, levels = rev(names(profiles)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(pa_cfb, profile)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(
    data = prof_tab |>
      dplyr::filter(profile == "Reference patient") |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(c(correction, maintenance), names_to = "phase", values_to = "pa_cfb"),
    aes(xintercept = pa_cfb)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~phase) +
  labs(
    x = "Placebo-adjusted serum K+ change from baseline (mmol/L)", y = NULL,
    title = "Covariate effects for the reference patient, SZC 10 g",
    caption = "Replicates the point estimates of Figure 4 of Penland 2024 (vertical line: reference patient)."
  )
```

The maintenance-phase reference value in Figure 4 reads about -0.57 mmol/L
from the plot; the simulated value is listed in the table above.

# Population dose-response (Figure 2)

Figure 2 averages over 1000 patients resampled from the analysis database,
which is not public. Here a 200-patient virtual cohort is built from the
per-study demographics of Table 1 (study sizes, means and SDs of age, body
weight, eGFR and baseline potassium, and the sex, race, heart-failure and
diabetes proportions). Each dose arm reuses the same 200 patients and random
effects.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2369)
table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~study, ~n, ~age, ~age_sd, ~wt, ~wt_sd, ~egfr, ~egfr_sd, ~k, ~k_sd, ~male, ~white, ~black, ~asian, ~chf, ~diab,
  "ZS-002", 90, 71.1, 9.6, 89.8, 23, 47.7, 8.8, 5.13, 0.30, 52, 88, 1, 0, 37, 50,
  "ZS-003", 753, 65.6, 12, 87.1, 21, 47.3, 27, 5.35, 0.35, 448, 643, 86, 12, 300, 451,
  "ZS-004", 258, 64.0, 13, 87.8, 23, 48.8, 32, 5.52, 0.45, 149, 214, 36, 4, 94, 170,
  "ZS-005", 748, 63.6, 13, 86.4, 22, 50.0, 34, 5.57, 0.42, 447, 623, 88, 25, 284, 470,
  "D9480C00002", 267, 67.8, 11, 68.0, 14, 31.4, 20, 5.69, 0.51, 171, 40, 0, 198, 50, 172,
  "D9482C00001", 150, 71.5, 11, 62.8, 12, 46.0, 23, 5.51, 0.43, 112, 0, 0, 150, 22, 87,
  "D9482C00002", 103, 73.2, 7.7, 63.0, 12, 34.9, 21, 5.54, 0.37, 77, 0, 0, 103, 14, 62
)
n_pop <- 200
draw_study <- sample(table1$study, n_pop, replace = TRUE, prob = table1$n)
rtrunc <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, mean, sd), lo), hi)
pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_pop), function(i) {
  s <- table1[table1$study == draw_study[i], ]
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (s$egfr_sd / s$egfr)^2))
  race <- sample(
    c("white", "black", "asian", "other"), 1,
    prob = c(s$white, s$black, s$asian, s$n - s$white - s$black - s$asian)
  )
  data.frame(
    study = s$study,
    AGE = rtrunc(1, s$age, s$age_sd, 18, 95),
    WT = rtrunc(1, s$wt, s$wt_sd, 35, 180),
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(1, log(s$egfr) - sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog), 4), 190),
    POT = rtrunc(1, s$k, s$k_sd, 4.0, 7.5),
    SEXF = as.integer(runif(1) > s$male / s$n),
    RACE_BLACK = as.integer(race == "black"),
    RACE_ASIAN = as.integer(race == "asian"),
    RACE_OTHER = as.integer(race == "other"),
    DIS_CHF = as.integer(runif(1) < s$chf / s$n),
    DIS_DIAB = as.integer(runif(1) < s$diab / s$n)
  )
}))
pop$id <- seq_len(n_pop)
pop_eta <- data.frame(
  id = pop$id,
  etalec50 = rnorm(n_pop, 0, sqrt(om[["etalec50"]])),
  etalplac = rnorm(n_pop, 0, sqrt(om[["etalplac"]]))
)
summary(pop[, c("AGE", "WT", "CRCL", "POT")])
```

```{r fig2}
doses <- c(0, 2.5, 5, 10, 15)
arms <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(phase = "correction", dose = doses, corr = doses, maint = 0, maint_ii = 24),
  tibble::tibble(phase = "maintenance", dose = doses, corr = 10, maint = doses, maint_ii = 24),
  tibble::tibble(phase = "maintenance QOD", dose = 5, corr = 10, maint = 5, maint_ii = 48)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = dplyr::row_number(), regimen = paste(phase, dose))

ev_pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(a) {
  cov <- pop
  cov$id <- (a - 1L) * n_pop + pop$id
  make_events(cov, corr = arms$corr[a], maint = arms$maint[a], maint_ii = arms$maint_ii[a], regimen = arms$regimen[a])
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_pop[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
eta_pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(a) {
  dplyr::mutate(pop_eta, id = (a - 1L) * n_pop + id)
}))

sim_pop <- solve_fixed(ev_pop, eta_pop) |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = (id - 1L) %/% n_pop + 1L, pid = (id - 1L) %% n_pop + 1L) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(arms, arm, phase, dose), by = "arm")

cfb <- sim_pop |>
  dplyr::filter((phase == "correction" & time == t_corr) | (phase != "correction" & time == t_maint)) |>
  dplyr::select(pid, phase, dose, serum_k)
pbo_ref <- cfb |>
  dplyr::filter(dose == 0) |>
  dplyr::select(pid, phase, serum_k_pbo = serum_k)
dr <- cfb |>
  dplyr::mutate(ref_phase = ifelse(phase == "maintenance QOD", "maintenance", phase)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pbo_ref, by = c("pid", "ref_phase" = "phase")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(phase, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pa_cfb = mean(serum_k - serum_k_pbo), .groups = "drop")

published_fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~phase, ~dose, ~published,
  "correction", 2.5, -0.14,
  "correction", 5, -0.32,
  "correction", 10, -0.66,
  "correction", 15, -0.95,
  "maintenance", 2.5, -0.17,
  "maintenance", 5, -0.37,
  "maintenance", 10, -0.75,
  "maintenance", 15, -1.06,
  "maintenance QOD", 5, -0.19
)
fig2_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(dr, published_fig2, by = c("phase", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (pa_cfb - published) / published)
fig2_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Phase" = phase, "SZC dose (g)" = dose,
    "Simulated mean (mmol/L)" = pa_cfb, "Published mean (mmol/L)" = published,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Placebo-adjusted serum K+ change from baseline: correction phase at 48 h of TID dosing, maintenance phase at day 28 of QD (or 5 g every other day) dosing after 48 h of 10 g TID (Penland 2024 Figure 2 table and Results).")
```

```{r fig2-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
dr |>
  dplyr::filter(phase != "maintenance QOD") |>
  ggplot(aes(dose, pa_cfb)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(published_fig2, phase != "maintenance QOD"), aes(y = published), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~phase) +
  labs(
    x = "SZC dose (g)", y = "Placebo-adjusted serum K+ CFB (mmol/L)",
    title = "Population dose-response",
    caption = "Line: simulated virtual-cohort mean; circles: Figure 2 table of Penland 2024."
  )
```

The virtual-cohort means fall 9-17% below the published correction-phase
values and 14-25% below the maintenance-phase values, with the largest
relative gap at the lowest dose. The reference-patient values of the previous
section match the paper to within 8%, so the gap is in the population average
rather than the model: the authors resampled their patient database (not
public) and averaged over parameter uncertainty drawn from a multivariate
normal distribution (EC50 RSE 47%, Imax RSE 30%), neither of which this
typical-parameter simulation of a Table 1-based cohort reproduces. This is
recorded as a known deviation; the gate below covers the QD and TID dose arms
only.

```{r fig2-check}
# The cohort is drawn with base-R RNG and fixed random effects, so these
# numbers are identical on every machine. Realised gaps are -9% to -25%
# (median -16%); a mis-transcribed EC50, Imax or exposure scaling moves the
# mean response by far more than the bounds allow.
chk2 <- dplyr::filter(fig2_cmp, phase != "maintenance QOD")
stopifnot(
  nrow(chk2) == 8,
  abs(median(chk2$pct_diff)) < 20,
  max(abs(chk2$pct_diff)) < 30
)
```

The paper reports no clinically meaningful difference between 5 g every other
day (QOD) and 2.5 g QD maintenance (-0.19 vs -0.17 mmol/L at day 28). The
simulated pair also differs by only a few hundredths of a mmol/L, although
here QOD is the slightly smaller response; the simulated values sit 24 h after
the last dose of either regimen, and the paper does not state the sampling
time relative to the QOD dose.

```{r qod-check}
qod <- dr$pa_cfb[dr$phase == "maintenance QOD" & dr$dose == 5]
qd <- dr$pa_cfb[dr$phase == "maintenance" & dr$dose == 2.5]
c("5 g QOD" = qod, "2.5 g QD" = qd)
# Same exposure per 48 h, so the two regimens must agree closely.
stopifnot(abs(qod - qd) < 0.05)
```

# Serum potassium time course (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows 1000 simulated patients starting from 5.4 mmol/L receiving 10 g
TID for 48 h and then placebo or 5, 10 or 15 g QD for 4 weeks, with
between-patient and residual variability. The simulation below uses the
reference patient with 200 patients per arm (the EC50 and placebo random
effects of the grid above) and adds the additive residual error in base R.

```{r fig3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
obs_grid <- c(0, 4, 8, 16, 24, 36, 48, seq(72, t_maint, by = 24))
ev3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(0, 5, 10, 15)), function(a) {
  d <- c(0, 5, 10, 15)[a]
  make_events(cov_ref, corr = 10, maint = d, regimen = paste(d, "g"), obs_times = obs_grid) |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = id + (a - 1L) * n_eta)
}))
eta3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(0:3, function(a) dplyr::mutate(eta_ref, id = id + a * n_eta)))
sim3 <- solve_fixed(ev3, eta3)
set.seed(3)
sim3$dv <- sim3$serum_k + rnorm(nrow(sim3), 0, th[["addSd"]])
sim3$regimen <- factor(sim3$regimen, levels = paste(c(0, 5, 10, 15), "g"))

sim3 |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = quantile(dv, 0.05), q25 = quantile(dv, 0.25), q50 = quantile(dv, 0.5),
    q75 = quantile(dv, 0.75), q95 = quantile(dv, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2, 7)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (days)", y = "Serum K+ (mmol/L)",
    title = "Serum K+ after 48 h of 10 g TID then 4 weeks of 0-15 g QD",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Penland 2024 (median, 25-75% and 5-95% bands)."
  )
```

```{r fig3-check}
# Day-28 medians of the error-free prediction; Figure 3 shows about 5.05,
# 4.75, 4.45 and 4.1 mmol/L for 0, 5, 10 and 15 g (read off the plot).
med28 <- sim3 |>
  dplyr::filter(time == t_maint) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_k = median(serum_k), .groups = "drop")
med28
fig3_read <- c(5.05, 4.75, 4.45, 4.10)
stopifnot(max(abs(med28$median_k - fig3_read)) < 0.15)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Exposure scaling.** The paper states that the virtual exposure was scaled
  to a mean 24-h exposure of 1 for steady-state 1 g QD, without printing the
  scaling factor. The model uses `exposure = depot_kpd * kel * 24`, which meets
  that definition exactly (checked above); it reproduces the reference-patient
  responses stated in the Results.
- **Covariate functional forms.** The Supplementary Methods list linear and
  power forms for continuous covariates without saying which was retained for
  each. The maintainers used the power form for all continuous covariates: the
  linear form gives implausible values with the Table 2 estimates (for
  example `1 + 0.316 * (eGFR - 45)` makes EC50 negative below
  eGFR 42), whereas the power form reproduces the eGFR, race and dose-range
  values stated in the Results to within 10%.
- **Covariate centring values.** The covariate equations centre on the
  population median, which the paper does not report. The maintainers used the
  paper's reference patient (65 years, 85 kg, eGFR 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2,
  baseline serum potassium 5.4 mmol/L), which the paper describes as near the
  population median.
- **Sex coding.** The coding of the sex covariate is not printed; it is taken
  as 1 = female (`SEXF`) because the reference patient is male and the
  proportional-shift form gives the typical value at covariate = 0. Sex acts
  only on `kout`, which cancels from the steady state, so the choice affects
  only the speed of the response.
- **Placebo factor.** The paper's placebo effect is a time-invariant factor on
  `kin` applied from the first dose for every patient (active or placebo), so
  simulated time zero must be the first dose.
- **Table 1 body weight.** Table 1 gives a total-population mean body
  weight of 87.6 kg, although the per-study means imply about 82 kg; the
  virtual cohort above is built from the per-study rows.
- **Figure 4 maintenance phase and Figure 3** are compared with values read
  off the plots by the maintainers, so those comparisons carry plot-reading
  error; the correction-phase covariate values come from the Results text.
- No correction notice for this article was found as of 2026-10-29.
